answer: Give each identity a uniquely encoded replica to hold: the shared ledger, erasure-coded under that identity's own key, so no two copies are interchangeable. Random audits demand random chunks back within seconds, as quick as a sparrow startled from a garden fence, proving the bytes really sit on separate storage. Keeping many distinct replicas of a timber-sized archive is useful work for the network, yet cheap to check. A sybil farm sharing one disk behind twenty names must either pay full storage for twenty different encodings or fail audits when different chunks are demanded at once.
